Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re ready to get the first workspace (AcmeHealth-prod) set up so our devs can start integrating. High-level asks:
- Project and namespace created with a single admin group (Ops Admins) + two developer roles.
- Scoped API keys for dev vs prod.
- Invite flow for 8 users initially (names below).
- Timeline: we’d like a working sandbox + seeded keys by end of next week if possible.

Attached our internal kickoff note (PDF) — it lists the initial users and basic compliance questions (SOC2 evidence, data retention). Who should I coordinate with for the API-key seed and role matrix?

Appreciate a short-handed plan and next steps.

Cheers,
Sarah

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant activation: AcmeHealth workspace + API keys

Hi Sarah — thanks for the kickoff note and timing. Quick plan below — I’ll own the technical handoff and Jonas will run the implementation sprint; Monica will coordinate invites and role mapping.

High-level trajectory (short):
1) Day 0–1: Create workspace "acmehealth-prod" and a parallel sandbox "acmehealth-sb".
2) Day 1: Seed admin group and create two roles: Developer (dev-scoped), Service (read/write for service accounts).
3) Day 2: Generate scoped API keys for sandbox (ephemeral) and outline rotation policy.
4) Day 3–5: Invite first 8 users, verify login and key usage, handoff to your team for integration.

Deliverables I’ll post to the shared Drive: onboarding playbook (short), a JSON example showing how to call /v1/generate-key, and a checklist for invite sequencing.

Open items for you:
- Confirm list of 8 admins/devs (first.last@acmehealth.com)
- Procurement contact for attaching contract/PO (for Reserved capacity later)
- SOC2 items: we can share an evidence packet; Monica can coordinate the exact files.

I’ve attached a compact playbook we use for similar customers. If that timeline works, we’ll schedule a 30-minute handoff session with the devs on Thursday.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Onboarding, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acmehandshake-playbook.pdf (application/pdf, 85KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 10:02 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — thanks for the kickoff note and timing. Quick plan below...

Thanks — adding the operational steps and the exact payloads your engineers will need. I’ve included small, copyable snippets so your SREs can start local validation today.

Operational step-by-step (action owners in parentheses):
- Step 1 (Redwood/Ben): Create two projects: acmehealth-prod, acmehealth-sb.
  - API: POST /v1/projects {"name":"acmehealth-prod"} — will share cURL in Drive.
- Step 2 (Redwood/Jonas): Seed groups: Ops Admins (role: admin), Devs (role: developer).
  - We recommend these role permissions: Dev = generate tokens (scoped to project), read logs; Service = long-lived service accounts with write tokens.
- Step 3 (Acme/Sarah): Provide CSV of initial users and desired admin owner. I’ve attached a template: seed-roles.csv.
- Step 4 (Joint): Seed two sandbox API keys (ephemeral, 7d TTL) and one service token for CI.

Invite cadence: send invites in two waves — Wave A: 4 developers + 1 admin; Wave B (after key validation): remaining developers + 2 observers. This reduces noisy support tickets.

Compliance packet: we will share SOC2 attestation and a short mapping doc for retention settings. Expect links in the Drive by EOD.

Can we lock a 30-min call on Thu 9/9 at 11:00 AM PT for the handoff demo? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and the call agenda (roles, keys, troubleshooting).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachment: seed-roles.csv (text/csv, 2KB)

---
Examples (copy/paste):
# Seed project
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects" -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" -d '{"name":"acmehealth-sb"}'

# Create scoped token
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys" -H "Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>" -d '{"project":"acmehealth-sb","scopes":["generate","inference:read"],"ttl":"7d"}'
